بَرُودٌ : see بَارِدٌ. ―
-b2- Beverage that cools the heat of thirst. (T.) ―
-b3- Also, (T, L, K,) and ↓ مَبْرُودٌ , (T, M, A, L, K,) Bread upon which water is poured; (T, L, K;) which is moistened with cold water: (A:) eaten by women to make them fat. (M, A, L.) The subst. applied to such bread is ↓ بَرِيدٌ (A.) ―
-b4- بَرُودٌ [as an epithet in which the quality of a subst. predominates] also signifies Cold water which one pours upon his head. (M.) ―
-b5- Anything with which a thing is rendered cold, or cooled. (S, M.) ―
-b6- A collyrium which cools the eye; (Lth, T, M, Msb;) also termed بَرُودُ العَيْنِ. (T, S.) ―
-b7- بَرُودُ الظِّلِّ (assumed tropical:) Pleasant in social intercourse: applied alike to the male and the female. (TA, from a trad.) ―
-b8- ثَوْبٌ بَرُودٌ A garment without nap: (K:) and a garment that is not warm nor soft. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
